title: De la Espriella Suspends Transition After Petro Refuses to Recognize Election Result
detail: President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella suspended the formal government handover ('empalme') after outgoing President Gustavo Petro refused to recognize his June 21 runoff victory and repeated fraud accusations without providing evidence. De la Espriella wrote on X that the transition process would be suspended immediately with what he called 'the corrupt government.' Finance Minister Germán Ávila responded that 'the transition process is not a criminal investigation; it is not a trial. We have absolutely nothing to hide.' The European Union observer mission and the Carter Center both confirmed the results management system was reliable, transparent and fully traceable, with de la Espriella's roughly 251,000-vote margin standing.

media.caption: Colombia's president-elect suspends transition after Petro alleges fraud

title: De la Espriella Names Commerce, Housing, and Sports Ministers
detail: President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella named three more cabinet ministers: Mauricio Gómez Amin (Commerce, Industry and Tourism), his former campaign manager and a Barranquilla-born attorney and ex-Senator; Jaime Andrés Beltrán (Housing), a communications specialist, evangelical pastor, and former mayor of Bucaramanga whose own election had been annulled by the Council of State; and Juliana Gutiérrez (Sports), sister of Medellín Mayor Federico Gutiérrez and a Creemos movement campaign coordinator who helped secure Antioquia's support.

media.caption: De la Espriella names Amin, Beltrán, and Gutiérrez to cabinet
